movement.unit: from/to in percent; delta in basis points

basis: Group net interest margin for the full year ended 30 June 2021 versus the full year ended 30 June 2020, on a continuing-operations basis and associated with the bank's cash-basis net interest income presentation. Evidence: (CBA-FY21-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF page 32, "Net interest income - \"cash basis\""); (CBA-FY21-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF page 32, "Average interest earning assets is presented on a continuing operations basis"); (CBA-FY21-results-presentation.pdf, PDF page 63, "Presented on a continuing operations basis."); (CBA-FY20-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF page 32, "Net interest margin (%) 2.07").

drivers.name: Higher liquid assets
drivers.narrative: Higher lower-yielding non-lending interest-earning assets, including liquid assets, reduced Group NIM. CBA also disclosed that average liquid asset balances increased by $17 billion, mainly because of strong customer deposit growth.
citations: (CBA-FY21-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF page 32, "Liquid assets: Decreased margin by 4 basis points")
(CBA-FY21-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF page 32, "a $17 billion increase in average liquid asset balances mainly due to strong customer deposit growth")
(CBA-FY21-results-presentation.pdf, PDF page 63, "Higher Liquids (4)")

drivers.name: Asset pricing
drivers.narrative: Business lending margins reduced NIM by 1 bp following repricing to support businesses during COVID-19, and consumer-finance margins reduced it by 1 bp as the share of interest-earning credit-card balances fell. Home-lending margins were flat: repricing added 9 bp, offset by variable-to-fixed switching of 5 bp and competition of 4 bp.
citations: (CBA-FY21-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF page 32, "Asset pricing: Decreased margin by 2 basis points")
(CBA-FY21-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF page 32, "lower business lending margins (down 1 basis point)")
(CBA-FY21-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF page 32, "lower consumer finance margins (down 1 basis point)")
(CBA-FY21-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF page 32, "repricing (up 9 basis points)")
(CBA-FY21-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF page 32, "variable rate to fixed rate loans (down 5 basis points)")
(CBA-FY21-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF page 32, "increased competition (down 4 basis points)")

drivers.name: Deposit pricing and funding costs
drivers.narrative: Lower earnings on transaction and savings deposits following cash-rate reductions reduced NIM by 7 bp. A 2 bp replicating-portfolio benefit and 2 bp from lower wholesale funding costs partly offset that pressure, producing the disclosed 3 bp net drag.
citations: (CBA-FY21-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF page 32, "Funding costs: Decreased margin by 3 basis points")
(CBA-FY21-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF page 32, "decreases in the cash rate (down 7 basis points)")
(CBA-FY21-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF page 32, "replicating portfolio (up 2 basis points)")
(CBA-FY21-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF page 32, "lower wholesale funding costs (up 2 basis points)")

drivers.name: Portfolio mix
drivers.narrative: Funding mix added 4 bp as the average deposit-funding ratio rose to 77% from 71%, transaction and savings deposits grew, customers shifted to at-call deposits, and CBA drew the Term Funding Facility. A 2 bp adverse asset-mix effect, mainly the decline in higher-margin consumer-finance balances, left a 2 bp net benefit.
citations: (CBA-FY21-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF page 33, "Portfolio mix: Increased margin by 2 basis points")
(CBA-FY21-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF page 33, "30 June 2021: 77%; 30 June 2020: 71%")
(CBA-FY21-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF page 33, "the drawdown of the TFF (up 4 basis points)")
(CBA-FY21-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF page 33, "an unfavourable impact from asset mix (down 2 basis points)")

drivers.name: Basis risk
drivers.narrative: A decrease in the average spread between the three-month bank-bill swap rate and the three-month overnight-index swap rate increased NIM, despite structurally lower exposure from growth in cash-rate-linked deposits and the shift toward fixed-rate home loans.
citations: (CBA-FY21-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF page 33, "The Bank’s margin increased 3 basis points reflecting a decrease in the average spread")
(CBA-FY21-results-presentation.pdf, PDF page 63, "Basis Risk (incl RP) 3")

drivers.name: Capital and other
drivers.narrative: Lower earnings on Group capital in the falling-rate environment reduced NIM by 3 bp. A 1 bp higher contribution from New Zealand, reflecting lower wholesale funding costs and favourable portfolio mix partly offset by RBNZ rate cuts, reduced the net drag to 2 bp.
citations: (CBA-FY21-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF page 33, "Capital and other: Decreased margin by 2 basis points")
(CBA-FY21-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF page 33, "lower earnings on Group capital due to the falling interest rate environment (down 3 basis points)")
(CBA-FY21-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF page 33, "increased contribution from New Zealand (up 1 basis point)")

drivers.name: Treasury and Markets
drivers.narrative: Higher bonds and commodities-financing income in Global Markets increased Group NIM.
citations: (CBA-FY21-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF page 33, "Treasury and Markets: Increased margin by 2 basis points")
(CBA-FY21-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF page 33, "higher bonds and commodities financing income in Global Markets")

limitations: Confidence scores are the analyst's requested probabilities, not figures reported by CBA.
The attribution is CBA's management bridge, with effects rounded to whole basis points; the zero residual is therefore a reconciliation on the disclosed rounded basis.
The documents do not provide a separate statutory-NIM bridge. The selected basis is the Group NIM shown with cash-basis net interest income and explicitly identified as continuing operations.

The profit announcement and presentation use slightly different sub-grouping for some lower-rate effects, but their parent categories and total movement reconcile; no numerical disagreement was found.
